newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish court convicts bikers for gang murder.
newsitem.headline: Danish court convicts bikers for gang murder.

text.p: A Danish jury on Friday found two members of the Hell's Angels motorcycle gang guilty of murdering the leader of the rival Bandidos and attempting to kill his companions in an ambush last March at the city's international airport.

The airport shooting turned a festering vendetta between the Hell's Angels and the Bandidos into full-blooded war in which the rivals have blasted each other with machine-guns, hand grenades, bombs and anti-tank missiles across the Nordic region.

Concluding a six-week trial conducted amid the tightest security ever seen at a Danish court, the jury found 23-year-old Michael Brokside and 34-year-old Joergen Nielsen guilty of murder and five counts of attempted murder.
It convicted Kim Jensen, 29, and Ove Witthoeft, 32, each of three counts of attempted murder but found Johnny Nielsen and Svend "The Swine' Holst innocent.
All six remained impassive as the verdicts were read out, eyewitnesses said.
Sentencing was expected later on Friday evening.
During the trial spectators were screened by a metal detector and scrutinised by officers familiar with the gangs, ready to weed out known bikers with criminal records.

Streets around the building were closed to traffic, court officials -- including the three judges -- wore special security badges and police bomb experts and their dogs swept the court before each sitting.
Cleaning staff were specially vetted and were watched by police as they worked.
The biker feud claimed its first life in February 1994, when a member of the Hell's Angels-affiliated Rednecks died in a gunfight with Bandidos in the Swedish port of Helsingborg.
Two more Bandidos died over the following two years, in Sweden and in Finland, but on March 10 this year the fighting took on a new intensity.

Gunmen outside Copenhagen International airport shot dead Danish Bandidos leader Uffe Larsen and wounded three of his companions as they waited to meet fellow-members returning from a visit to Helsinki.
At almost the same time, an attacker in Norway shot and wounded a Bandido arriving at Oslo's Fornebu airport. Police arrested a member of a Hell's Angels-allied gang.
A Danish Bandido was shot dead newar the Norwegian city of Drammen in July.

Last October, as Danish legislators put the finishing touches to legislation to clamp down on the warring gangs, attackers fired an anti-tank missile into Hell's Angels central Copenhagen clubhouse while it was packed with partygoers.
A gang member and a woman party guest died in the blast.
